CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit post bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female presenting for follow-up evaluation post bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on October 10, 2020. She reports that her breasts are healing well with no current breast-related complaints. Back pain, which was a primary indication for surgery, has completely resolved. She denies fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting. In March, PA Ruth Sanchez noted a lump under the left breast; however, the patient has not palpated this since that time and has been performing self-massage. Patient initially experienced bothersome scars and began daily application of scar gel. She does not feel she needs the gel as frequently now. Overall, patient is doing well and reports enjoying the summer.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, vomiting. Denies current lumps, bumps, or hard spots. Reports complete resolution of back pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty (October 10, 2020)

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel - topical application

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Patient reports family is in good health. Specific medical history not elicited.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying summertime. Otherwise doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Bilateral reduction mammoplasty incisions well-healed with no evidence of infection or erythema. Some scar widening noted, particularly at one incision site. No palpable lumps, masses, or hard spots. Previously noted lump not currently appreciated on examination. Overall satisfactory healing.

RESULTS
Clinical photographs obtained for documentation and monitoring.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty with overall satisfactory healing. Mild scar widening noted on examination.
2. Reassured that previously noted lump is likely scar tissue and not concerning.
3. Continue Mederma scar gel twice daily to affected areas; can also apply to other scars as needed.
4. Continue massage to surgical sites to help with scar appearance.
5. Discussed surgical scar revision (excision and reclosure) as option but deferred until at least one year post-operative.
6. Return to clinic in 6 months for reassessment of scars and healing.
7. Clinical photographs obtained today for ongoing monitoring.
